title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 293
paragraphs: At the banquets of the rich among them, when they have finished eating, a man bears round a wooden figure of a dead body in a coffin, made as like the reality as possible both by painting and by carving, and measuring about a cubit or two cubits each way. This he shows to each of those drinking together, saying: “When you look upon this, drink and be merry, for you shall be such as this when you are dead.” Thus they do at their carousals.
